<thought>Based on the NMR data, the compound has a para‑disubstituted benzene ring (two aromatic doublets each integrating to 2 H) and a cyclohexyl group (10 H at ~1.3 ppm and a benzylic CH at ~2.6 ppm). The total carbon count is 12, matching a phenyl ring (6 C) plus a cyclohexyl ring (6 C). The fourth substituent must be a non‑hydrogen atom that does not add carbon; a halogen (Cl, Br, F) fits this pattern. A plausible structure is para‑chlorocyclohexylbenzene, whose SMILES is “Clc1ccc(C2CCCCC2)cc1”. This SMILES satisfies the observed spectra and carbon count.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(C2CCCCC2)cc1</final_answer>
